hero.title: Hobby Gold Prospecting Switzerland
hero.subtitle: Follow the creek: from your first flake of gold to your own map of spots.

prospecting.title: The Joy of Gold Prospecting
prospecting.text: Gold prospecting means searching for the small flakes and nuggets that rivers have carried down from the Alps for thousands of years. All you need is a pan, some patience and a good creek. It gets you outdoors, teaches you to read the landscape, and every glint of gold in your pan is a small treasure you found yourself.

problem.title: Why a Modern Prospecting Tool?
problem.text: Knowing where to look is the hardest part. Information about gold-bearing rivers is scattered across old reports, forums and word of mouth, and your own findings often end up in a notebook or forgotten. Without a clear overview, it is hard to tell which spots are promising and which ones have already been tried.

map.title: A Map to Read the Rivers
map.text: The interactive map brings it all together. Draw your own prospecting areas, rate their gold presence, keep them private or share them with friends, and filter the map to spot the most promising places at a glance.

guide.title: A Guide for Beginners and Beyond
guide.text: New to prospecting? The guide explains where gold settles in a creek, how to pan step by step, where Swiss gold comes from and how to get started with metal detecting. Experienced prospectors will find tips to sharpen their eye for good spots.

legal.title: Prospect Legally, Leave No Trace
legal.text: In Switzerland every canton sets its own rules, and some communes add their own: where you may prospect, in which season and with which equipment. Know the regulations, respect protected areas and fish spawning periods, and leave every riverbank as you found it, so the hobby stays legal and nature stays intact.

guide.intro: In this guide you will learn where and how to find gold. You will learn how gold finds its way into a river and which indicators are important.

whereToFind.title: Where to find the gold
whereToFind.text: Gold is most often found in rivers and streams where the current slows down, allowing the heavy metal to settle.
items: Inside bends of a river, where the flow is weakest.
Behind large boulders that break the current.
In cracks and crevices of the bedrock.

howToPan.title: How to pan for gold
howToPan.text: Fill your pan with gravel, submerge it, and swirl gently so lighter material washes away while the gold sinks to the bottom.
steps: Scoop gravel into the pan and remove the largest rocks.
Submerge the pan and shake it side to side to settle the gold.
Tilt and swirl to wash off the lighter sediment.
Repeat until only the heavy black sand and gold remain.

origin.title: Where the gold comes from
origin.text: Gold originates deep within the earth and is carried to the surface by geological activity, then eroded into rivers over time.
